subsystems.name: Unit cell geometry
subsystems.role: the repeating shape that sets the bulk mechanical response.

subsystems.name: Base material
subsystems.role: provides intrinsic strength, stiffness and density.

subsystems.name: Design and simulation software
subsystems.role: predicts and optimises behaviour before manufacture.

subsystems.name: Integration and interface
subsystems.role: attaches the lattice to the rest of the product.

subsystems.name: Testing and characterisation
subsystems.role: verifies stiffness, strength and energy absorption.

buildSteps.title: Set the performance target
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether the part must absorb impact, be stiff and light, or deform in a specific way such as a negative Poisson's ratio.

buildSteps.title: Design the unit cell
buildSteps.detail: Create a repeating geometry — for example a re-entrant honeycomb — using CAD, aiming at the target property.

buildSteps.title: Simulate and optimise
buildSteps.detail: Finite element analysis predicts how the lattice will deform; the geometry is adjusted iteratively.

buildSteps.title: Select the base material
buildSteps.detail: Choose a polymer, metal or ceramic whose intrinsic properties suit the application and the chosen printing process.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the lattice
buildSteps.detail: Additive manufacturing builds the struts and nodes layer by layer; alternatively, a mould or template can be used for foams.

buildSteps.title: Post-process
buildSteps.detail: Remove support material, cure, heat-treat or coat the part to reach final properties.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into the product
buildSteps.detail: Bond or mechanically lock the lattice into the surrounding structure, such as a helmet liner or shoe midsole.

buildSteps.title: Test and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Mechanical tests and CT scans check that the manufactured lattice matches the design, and the geometry is refined.

prerequisites.why: only 3D printing can routinely build the fine, complex internal geometry of a lattice at small scales.
the behaviour of thousands of cells cannot be predicted by hand; FEA and optimisation are essential.
the lattice is only as good as the solid it is made from, whether resin, titanium or ceramic.
geometries such as re-entrant honeycombs are understood well enough to design negative Poisson's ratio behaviour on purpose.

pathway.milestone: niche commercial products such as 3D-printed shoe midsoles and impact-absorbing helmet liners
wider use in aerospace and automotive lightweighting
pathway.unlocks: fuel and material savings in transport.

pathway.milestone: multifunctional metamaterials that combine stiffness with heat exchange or acoustic damping
pathway.unlocks: single parts that do several jobs at once.

pathway.milestone: programmable or adaptive metamaterials whose properties change on demand
pathway.unlocks: structures that can reconfigure themselves for different loads or conditions.
